args.question:
Is the `detected_at` semantics change in `src/sampled_audit_loop.py` a blocking
finding, or is it in scope and acceptable as written?

I can verify what the code does — it writes `sample.merged_at` where it
previously wrote `sample.audited_at`. What I cannot resolve mechanically is
whether shipping that without touching the 41 rows already in the ledger is
acceptable, or whether it silently corrupts the very trend this issue exists to
produce. That is a judgment call about the ledger's contract, so I am asking
rather than deciding.
args.context:
Established so far in this review:

1. The diff is 4 files, +96/-9, on issue #9812 (weekly escape digest on the
   Insights tab). Two of the four files are additive and read-only; the third is
   `src/sampled_audit_loop.py`, a caretaker loop.
2. `_record_upheld` previously wrote `sample.audited_at` into
   `EscapeRecord.detected_at`. It now writes `sample.merged_at`. I confirmed both
   fields exist on `AuditSample` (`src/audit/models.py:41`) and that nothing else
   reads `detected_at` except `build_digest`.
3. `escape_ledger.jsonl` currently holds 41 rows, all written under the old
   meaning. ADR-0021 makes the ledger append-only with no migration mechanism, so
   those rows cannot be rewritten.
4. `build_digest` buckets on `detected_at` with no way to tell which meaning a
   row was written under. So the first ~10 weeks of the chart are audit-time
   buckets and everything after the merge is merge-time buckets, mixed in one
   series with no visual or structural break.
5. The shaped direction on #9812 explicitly asked for this change and the product
   owner said "say so in the PR body, because anyone reading the ledger
   afterwards needs to know the column changed meaning". The PR body does not
   mention it.
6. The executor's own verdict summary lists this as "dismissed as intentional and
   specified".

What I have not established: whether 41 mixed rows is materially misleading at
the granularity this panel renders (weekly, ~4 escapes/week), or whether the
right call is to accept it and document the cut-over.
options: Blocking. The trend is the deliverable and a series that silently mixes two time axes is a wrong answer rather than an incomplete one. Require a marker on the record (e.g. a `time_basis` field on new rows) so `build_digest` can separate or exclude the old rows.

Blocking, but cheaper: accept the mixed rows and require the digest to start its window at the cut-over date, so the panel only ever charts one meaning. Costs the first 10 weeks of history, which nobody has been able to read anyway.
Concern, not blocking. Accept as written, require the PR body to state the cut-over as the product owner asked, and file a follow-up to backfill or annotate the 41 existing rows.
Not a finding. At ~4 escapes/week over weekly buckets the audit-vs-merge skew is under one bucket for most rows, so the mixed series is not materially misleading and the change is specified.
